title: Marketplace fees + revrec sensitivity analysis (AWS/GCP) — v2
body:
Workbook purpose
- Quantify margin impact of AWS & GCP marketplace fees across Redwood Marketplace SKUs (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private + add-ons).
- Flag revenue recognition considerations (ASC 606) that affect reporting (gross vs net, timing, contract modifications, refunds/credits).
- Recommend floor pricing + discount guardrails for marketplace deals so we don’t accidentally price below target contribution margin after fee + support burden.

IMPORTANT / DATA QUALITY
- Fee rates vary by marketplace program, contract structure, and partner-negotiated terms; use ranges and update once partner team confirms final terms in portal.
- This analysis assumes Redwood is a SaaS sold via marketplace for Hosted API and marketplace-sold commitments for Dedicated/Private where applicable. Private/on-prem licensing may require direct paper depending on marketplace constraints; see “Policy recs” tab.

TAB: Inputs (editable)
Field	Value	Notes
Analysis version	v2	Updated for SKU catalog v2 + add-ons
Assumed marketplace fee rate (AWS)	3.0% to 5.0%	Use 3% base case; run 5% high-case
Assumed marketplace fee rate (GCP)	3.0% to 5.0%	Use 3% base case; run 5% high-case
Payment terms (marketplace)	Net 30–60	Cash timing differs by marketplace; impacts working capital
Refund / dispute reserve	0.5% of GMV	Placeholder; adjust once we see real refund patterns
Support & CS burden uplift (marketplace)	+10% to +20%	More procurement + onboarding tickets; see Support readiness plan
Target contribution margin (Hosted API)	>= 65%	Post-inference COGS + fee + support
Target contribution margin (Dedicated)	>= 45%	After infra + fee + support + onboarding
Target contribution margin (Private)	>= 55%	Software fee typically high margin, but heavier onboarding + security review time
Add-on attach assumptions (for modeling only)	Compliance 25%, Retention 15%, Premium SLA 10%	Do not treat as forecast; used for blended fee impact

TAB: SKU summary (from packaging v2; finance interpretation)
SKU family	Charge type	Meter/Unit	Typical procurement mode	Revrec notes (high level)
Hosted API	Usage-based	Tokens/requests/embeddings	Self-serve + enterprise spend	Variable consideration; revenue as usage occurs
Dedicated	Subscription / commit	Monthly or annual commit	Enterprise procurement	Over time; may include setup; watch for performance obligations
Private	Subscription / license	Annual platform fee (+ support)	Enterprise procurement	Over time; evaluate any separate implementation services
Compliance add-on	Subscription	Monthly/annual	Enterprise procurement	Over time; likely part of stand-ready obligation
Retention add-on	Subscription	Monthly/annual	Enterprise procurement	Over time; distinct service if separately priced
Premium SLA add-on	Subscription	Monthly/annual	Enterprise procurement	Over time; careful wording (SLA credits vs refund mechanics)

TAB: Fee impact scenarios (per $1,000,000 GMV)
Assumptions: fee applied to gross marketplace billed amount (GMV). Reserve is applied to GMV. Support uplift shown separately as a cost line.

Scenario	Marketplace fee rate	GMV	Marketplace fee ($)	Refund reserve ($)	Net proceeds before COGS ($)
Base	3.0%	1,000,000	30,000	5,000	965,000
High fee	5.0%	1,000,000	50,000	5,000	945,000
Stress	8.0%	1,000,000	80,000	5,000	915,000

Quick read:
- Every +1% marketplace fee reduces proceeds by $10,000 per $1M GMV.
- When deals are already discounted, the fee mechanically increases effective discount vs direct contracts.

TAB: Effective discount math (example)
Goal: show how marketplace fee interacts with discounts.

Inputs	Direct contract	Marketplace
List price (annual)	$1,000,000	$1,000,000
Negotiated discount	20%	20%
Customer price (GMV)	$800,000	$800,000
Marketplace fee rate	N/A	3%
Marketplace fee ($)	N/A	$24,000
Net to Redwood (before COGS)	$800,000	$776,000
Effective discount vs list	20.0%	22.4%

Interpretation:
- A “20% discount” in marketplace behaves like ~22–23% effective discount at a 3% fee (worse at 5%).
- If Sales targets a maximum effective discount, marketplace deals need either (a) smaller nominal discount, or (b) list uplift for marketplace only, or (c) shift to direct contract.

TAB: Floor pricing guidance (guardrails)
This tab converts target contribution margin into a max discount / minimum sell price guideline.

Definitions
- Unit economics vary by SKU; use blended contribution margins per SKU family and apply fee as a “cost of channel”.
- For Hosted usage-based SKUs, “discounts” may appear as (1) negotiated token rates, (2) committed spend with discounted overage, or (3) credits. Credits are economically similar to discount but may differ in revrec presentation.

Hosted API (usage-based) — recommended guardrails
Item	Recommendation	Rationale
Marketplace nominal discount cap	<= 15% off list (base case)	To keep effective discount <= ~18% after 3% fee
Exception path	Up to 25% only with VP Finance + Legal sign-off	Protect margin + avoid inconsistent precedent
Credits	Prefer “marketplace-native” constructs where possible; avoid large off-invoice credits without written approval	Credits complicate revrec and can be misunderstood by procurement
Minimum annualized GMV for custom pricing	$250k+ (marketplace)	Below this, support/procurement overhead dominates

Dedicated (commit) — recommended guardrails
Item	Recommendation	Rationale
Marketplace nominal discount cap	<= 10% off list	Dedicated already has thinner margin (infra reserved capacity)
Term length	Prefer 12 months+	Improves payback + reduces churn risk
Implementation / onboarding	If material, separate SOW via direct contract where possible	Marketplace may not support SOW cleanly; revrec separation is harder

Private (license) — recommended guardrails
Item	Recommendation	Rationale
Marketplace nominal discount cap	<= 15% off list	Private is strategic but can become services-heavy
Security/compliance add-ons	Do not “throw in” for free without Finance approval	Add-ons cost engineering/support + set precedent
Proof of concept	Prefer time-boxed paid pilot or direct paper	Marketplace refunds/disputes are operationally messy

TAB: Revrec notes (ASC 606) — finance/legal working notes (not a formal memo)
1) Principal vs agent (gross vs net)
- Preliminary view: Redwood is the principal in providing inference services/software access; marketplaces act as a sales channel/payment processor.
- However, the legal contract flow and who is “merchant of record” can affect presentation and may require net reporting in some cases.
- Action: Legal (Michael) to confirm contract structure for AWS and GCP programs; Finance to confirm accounting policy with auditors.

2) Usage-based revenue (Hosted API)
- Revenue recognized as usage occurs (variable consideration). Marketplace reporting cadence can introduce a lag between usage month and cash receipt.
- If marketplace reports usage/billing after month-end, ensure we have a reliable usage cut and reconciliation process.
- Credits: If we issue promotional credits, assess whether they represent a price concession (reduce transaction price) and track breakage policy.

3) Commit + overage constructs
- If marketplace SKU is a committed spend with overage, treat commit as stand-ready obligation over the commit period, with usage-based variable component for overage.
- Watch for contract modifications when customers upgrade/downgrade or add add-ons mid-term (see PM-876).

4) Refunds, disputes, and SLA credits
- Marketplace terms may allow refunds or chargebacks. We should maintain a reasonable reserve and define an internal approval flow for refund requests.
- SLA credits: generally treated as variable consideration (reduce revenue) when probable. Ensure SLA credit policy is consistent across direct vs marketplace.

5) Multi-element arrangements (Private + add-ons + support)
- If add-ons are distinct and separately priced, likely separate performance obligations. If they are “included”, ensure pricing/packaging doesn’t create implied obligations that auditors will question.
- Implementation services (if any) should be clearly separated (or explicitly excluded) from marketplace SKU descriptions to avoid revrec complexity.

TAB: Recommendations (to align pricing, quoting, and marketplace reality)
1) Decide on strategy: marketplace parity vs marketplace uplift
Option A — Parity pricing (same list as direct)
- Pros: simpler messaging, fewer SKU variants.
- Cons: marketplace fee becomes an automatic margin haircut; pushes us to tighten discounting.

Option B — Marketplace-specific list uplift (e.g., +3–5%)
- Pros: protects margins; keeps effective discount similar.
- Cons: requires careful messaging; must be consistent across AWS/GCP listings + internal quote tooling; could confuse customers if they compare channels.

Finance recommendation (provisional):
- Keep list price parity initially (avoid launch risk), but implement tighter discount caps for marketplace deals + an exception process.
- Re-evaluate after 1–2 quarters of marketplace deal data; if marketplace becomes a meaningful channel, consider a marketplace uplift for new SKUs only.

2) Discounting policy (what Sales can approve)
Approval tier	Marketplace deal parameters	Approval required
Standard	Within nominal discount caps above; standard terms	AE + Sales Mgmt (existing process)
Exception 1	Exceeds cap by up to +5 pts OR includes one add-on bundled free	VP Sales + VP Finance
Exception 2	Exceeds cap by >5 pts OR requests custom refund language/side letters	CFO delegate + Legal

3) Avoid “credit gymnastics” in marketplace
- Prefer discounting via marketplace SKU price/commit where possible rather than large post-purchase credits in our own system.
- If we must use credits (e.g., to match a direct renewal), require a written approval and document revrec treatment.

4) Instrumentation requirements (so Finance can reconcile)
- Marketplace order ID / entitlement ID must flow to billing ledger (ENG-4406).
- Monthly reconciliation: Marketplace statement GMV vs Redwood usage/commit recognition.
- Reporting: separate tracking for AWS vs GCP fee impact and refund rates.

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm final AWS and GCP fee schedules for our program tiers (Partnerships owner to provide portal screenshots / contract excerpt).
- Clarify whether any SKUs will require private offers and what that changes for discounting + approvals.
- Define standard language for refunds and SLA credits on marketplace (Legal + Support + PMM alignment).
- Confirm upgrade/downgrade policy for marketplace buyers (PM-876) and whether it triggers contract modification accounting.

Change log
- 2025-01-14 (LB): Created v1 with preliminary fee ranges + discount math.
- 2025-01-28 (RM): Added effective discount table + policy guardrails per SKU family.
- 2025-02-06 (MG): Added principal vs agent notes + multi-element considerations; flagged need to confirm merchant-of-record details.
